core_obligations: Assume (1) and let Z -> Y be arbitrary; choose a surjective etale V -> Y with V a scheme (proof lines 1130-1132).
Draw the square comparing |V x_Y X| -> |V| with |Z x_Y X| -> |Z| and record that the horizontal arrows are open and surjective and that the comparison map is surjective (proof lines 1133-1145).
Conclude that the right vertical arrow is submersive, which is (2) (proof lines 1145-1147).
Note that (2) implies (1) immediately from the definitions (proof lines 1147-1148).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a representable morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S, universal submersiveness in the representable sense is equivalent to |Z x_Y X| -> |Z| being submersive for every morphism Z -> Y (source lines 1117-1127). The proof of (1) implies (2) chooses a surjective etale V -> Y, uses that V x_Y X -> V is universally submersive as a morphism of schemes, and compares the two squares of topological spaces: the horizontal arrows are open and surjective, the map |V x_Y X| -> |V| x_{|Z|} |Z x_Y X| is surjective, so submersiveness of the left vertical arrow forces submersiveness of the right one. The converse implication is immediate from the definitions.
